key_insight: High-speed video can be converted into physically consistent molten-pool surface flow fields by combining optical flow with physics-informed neural networks.
engineering_relevance: This enables better diagnosis and control of wire-arc DED bead shape, defect formation, and solidification behavior without requiring direct high-temperature flow sensors.
method: Homography-correct the oblique camera view and extract dense optical flow from high-speed video.
Use a PINN for quasi-steady pools to fit observed velocities while enforcing incompressible Navier-Stokes, no-penetration boundaries, and arc-forcing priors.
Extend to a phase-conditioned time-dependent PINN for periodic droplet-impact regimes to reconstruct cyclic flow evolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reconstruction on high-speed imaging from a GTAW-based wire-arc DED process under two distinct regimes: quasi-steady convection and periodic droplet impact.
watch_item: Results depend on accurate camera calibration, optical-flow quality, and correctly specified physics/forcing assumptions, which may be sensitive under extreme glare or highly transient events.
paper_title: Reconstruction of Molten Pool Flow Fields from High-Speed Video Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
